his_words: [Editorial citation key, not an authorial mathematical statement]
statement: The Pro notes distinguish source witnesses, external project excerpts and modern references. The stated archival evidence is a mixed sequence, not a continuously dated treatise.
reconstruction: The present run checks actual supplied sources. Unseen context packets and findings cards remain external leads; their earlier verdicts are not adopted. The 11 September 1967 letter dates that letter only.
check_reason: Citation conventions are retained; external endpoints are unavailable and are not counted as checked links.

his_words: Cond. équivalentes a) b) c) d)
statement: For a flat module M over a nonfield Dedekind domain A, the manuscript equates finite saturation of every finite submodule, exclusion of each A^(p), absence of K in each M_p, and a union of finite saturated submodules; separating A-linear forms suffice and are asserted necessary for countably generated M.
reconstruction: The equivalence is false: over Z, M=sum over primes p of (1/p)Z has all local p-heights bounded by one, but saturation of Z is the nonfinite module M. The surviving a–d and countable projectivity implications are separated in CL-SA02-501.
check_reason: The note identifies the hypotheses but stops at an unproved package; a hypothesis-checked counterexample refutes b,c⇒a,d. Pro/Codex ambiguity in the word before module does not rescue this example.

statement: Under finite saturation for B, the coordinate coalgebra of a flat affine group over a Dedekind domain, each finite submodule lies in a finite saturated subcoalgebra. The two one-sided coaction conditions must survive saturation.
reconstruction: Saturation is a kernel with torsionfree quotient; flatness gives the required tensor intersections. This implication uses the finite-saturation hypothesis itself, not the false equivalence in the preceding lemma.
check_reason: The deferred parenthesis is explicit. Unequal tildes are retained as a reading issue; the saturation argument is independently supplied.

statement: If the group is also of finite type and its coordinate module has the preceding finite-saturation property, a finite projective stable algebra-generating submodule yields a faithful linear representation after every base change.
reconstruction: Faithfulness means trivial kernel on every algebra-valued point; it does not imply surjectivity or faithful flatness onto the entire general linear group.
check_reason: The proof explicitly tests points over arbitrary A-algebras, and the finite-type assumption is present.

statement: Every affine group scheme over a field is an inverse limit of finite-type affine group schemes with faithfully flat transition maps.
reconstruction: Finite Hopf subalgebras and faithful flatness over Hopf subalgebras, rather than finite subcoalgebras alone, are needed for this reconstruction.
check_reason: The correction from inductive to projective and the explanation of strictness are explicit; topological-group limits on 91/98–102 are distinct.

statement: For a directed union B=colim B_i of finite projective saturated subcoalgebras, finite B-comodules factor through a B_i; comodules over B_i correspond to modules over U_i=B_i^∨, with the stated restriction transitions.
reconstruction: Factorization for a finite module uses finitely many coaction coefficients and preservation of injectivity by the saturated stages; coassociativity and counit give the U_i action.
check_reason: The dual-algebra mechanism and admissible categories are on the page. The first unclear category label is not used to change the definition.

statement: A finite comodule over these Dedekind coalgebra stages is a quotient of a comodule finite projective over the base. A relative variant assumes ordinary finite quasi-coherent modules have finite locally free covers.
reconstruction: A finite U_i-module admits a surjection U_i^r; U_i is finite projective as an A-module. The relative continuation must specify which S or S′ is the base.
check_reason: The finite-type input is written here, unlike the broader sentence on 90/16; the change of base letter remains a reading alarm.

statement: The identification of the module criterion with nonempty fibres of every irreducible component is explicitly restricted to G of finite type over the Dedekind base.
reconstruction: This is a scope correction to the quoted external finding, not an authentication of its unseen counterexample or a proof of the equivalence. Components after base extension and the module condition must be matched exactly.
check_reason: The finite-type phrase is explicit. An external refutation deleting it does not address this written assertion.

statement: The cancelled 90/14 proposition claims that the representation on a finite stable generating module maps G faithfully flatly onto Aut(N). The live 90/6 conclusion is only faithful representation.
reconstruction: The earlier run’s test G_m acting on span(1,t,t^-1) gives diag(1,z^-1,z), a proper closed subgroup of GL_3. Its algebra map kills an off-diagonal coordinate, so it cannot be faithfully flat.
check_reason: The whole stronger proposition is deleted. The counterexample is rechecked and applies to that withdrawn wording only.

statement: Under the stated finite locally free coalgebra-stage hypotheses, a quasi-coherent submodule F of a G-equivariant E has a smallest stable quasi-coherent envelope in E; flat base change is claimed to commute with it. Later versions use a G-linearized relatively ample invertible sheaf.
reconstruction: Different base, quasi-compactness and resolution hypotheses belong to different versions. Mere flatness of the coordinate coalgebra is insufficient; the finite-stage/projectivity hypotheses are retained.
check_reason: The envelope is nontrivial for an arbitrary submodule, not a submodule already known G-stable. The note correctly distinguishes this.

statement: 90/16 asserts a finite locally free equivariant quotient for every equivariant module although its hypothesis supplies such covers only for finite-type modules.
reconstruction: The earlier run’s counterexample is S=X=Spec(k), G trivial, E a countably infinite direct sum of k. Every map from k^r has finite-dimensional image. The finite-type formulation is the plausible repair, not an emendation.
check_reason: The literal unrestricted conclusion is false; the point example checks every stated hypothesis and does not attack 90/10–12.

his_words: Si S qu. cpt qu. sép.
statement: The drafts place quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness on different objects; one version involving S is deleted, and a later version requires covers by finite locally free base modules.
reconstruction: No single theorem is obtained by combining selected clauses from all drafts. Each surviving version is tracked with its hypotheses; scan order supplies no date.
check_reason: The cancellation and revised hypotheses are visible in the transcriptions and cannot be silently combined.

statement: For the relatively ample line bundle, the graded-section functor E↦⊕_n f_*(E⊗L^n) is left exact; graded sheafification is exact, left adjoint to sections, and its counit identifies the original quasi-coherent sheaf. Sections are therefore fully faithful in the specified setting.
reconstruction: This is the standard section/sheafification adjunction for the ample construction; it is unrelated merely by terminology to an external Lefschetz graded-ring programme.
check_reason: The two exactness assertions concern different functors and are not contradictory.

his_words: d’où par minimalité lui est égal
statement: The stable envelope of a graded submodule is the direct sum of the stable envelopes of its homogeneous pieces; functoriality with respect to multiplication then makes it a graded module over the section algebra.
reconstruction: The equality follows from two containments and minimality. Algebra-module stability is a second step, not a consequence of grading alone.
check_reason: The bracketed proof supplies this distinction; no missing index is silently added to the transcription.

statement: After twisting a finite-type F, finitely many sections generate it. The finite stable hull of their degree piece generates the proposed sheaf envelope, giving finite generation.
reconstruction: The equality with the minimal envelope uses stable generation and the two containments; the chosen sections and the ample-generation hypothesis must be retained.
check_reason: The rewriting request is explicit and is not evidence of a disproved argument.

his_words: F′ de F; F′ de E
statement: The first version places a containing stable envelope inside F; the later version places it in E and contains F.
reconstruction: The latter is the coherent mathematical formulation. The former is listed for scan review and is not edited.
check_reason: The two witnesses differ exactly in the ambient module.

statement: A flat local morphism of noetherian local rings with geometrically reduced fibres has connected generic fibre, and remains connected after deleting a closed subset above a proper closed base subset, when the base is geometrically unibranch, or unibranch with primary residue extension.
reconstruction: The reused EGA sheets include a punctured-spectrum reduction using depth. Missing inequality signs, the Japanese replacement and the formal-fibre corollary are kept separate.
check_reason: This is an independent EGA strand on the reused pages, not an equivariant-generation step.

statement: Under the hypotheses of the preceding EGA completion result, base change is fully faithful on all étale schemes. The separated target case is followed by descent of the open graph in the general case.
reconstruction: The extension from separated targets uses descent of the graph and descent of isomorphisms; it does not claim equivalence or essential surjectivity.
check_reason: Both the obsolete separated formulation and the general graph argument are supplied.

reconstruction: The uncertain marginal words remain uncertain. A noetherian profinite Hausdorff space is finite by compactness and discreteness; the corresponding ring assertion still needs its stated flat/injective transition hypotheses.

statement: A finitely presented group homomorphism with flat kernel has the represented quotient G/N and its monomorphism to the target under the preceding factorization hypotheses.

statement: For proper flat X,Z over S, a map i:Z→X and a separated finite-presentation target Y, precomposition Hom(X,Y)→Hom(Z,Y) is represented by unramified morphisms on the open locus where the infinitesimal restriction is injective, equivalently M_v→M_u is surjective.

check_reason: Later supplied Codex leaves were absent from the old note’s evidence. They must be incorporated; they do not by themselves erase every proof gap.

statement: The deformation Hom functors in a base module J are corepresented by coherent base modules, compatibly with base extension; precomposition induces M_v→M_u.
reconstruction: The coherent Hom functor represented by a vector-type affine scheme is related but not identical until its additivity identifies the corepresenting module. This identification is part of the reconstruction.
check_reason: The critical module construction is explicitly asserted; a fibre-dimension argument alone would not establish base-change compatibility.

statement: Once M_v→M_u is constructed, its surjectivity locus is the complement of the support of its finitely presented cokernel and is universal under base change.
reconstruction: The earlier run’s presentation-matrix test is rechecked: if A^n→A^m→C→0, the locus C=0 is the union of principal opens of all maximal m×m minors, with the usual conventions for m=0 and n<m.
check_reason: This proves the open-locus step conditionally on the modules; it is not a proof of the entire Hom theorem.

statement: The author asserts reductions to Artinian or noetherian bases, with a possible reservation in the margin. Pro and Codex differ in the local adjective.
reconstruction: Limit descent must carry X,Z,Y,i and the module map, including the surjectivity condition. The uncertain “sans doute” is not a secure independent objection.
check_reason: The reductions are asserted rather than proved and remain attached to their specific finite-presentation hypotheses.

statement: The lift problem over a nilpotent ideal compares pseudo-torsors with their acting Hom groups. Codex 19–21 admits compatibility equalities; 23–25 revises the obstruction quotient.
reconstruction: The earlier run’s algebraic square is valid when V→U is surjective and J→J_t injective: Hom(U,J)=Hom(V,J)×_{Hom(V,J_t)}Hom(U,J_t). Nonemptiness of the pseudo-torsors is an additional issue. The later quotient must use the image of the kernel of the compatibility map.
check_reason: The old assertion of no supplied continuation is corrected by reading Codex 19–25. A group-square identity does not establish existence of a point in an empty pseudo-torsor.

statement: The margin asks for a relative-product version and suggests that a nearby hypothesis can be omitted when Z→X is surjective; the later section-functor theorem and letter are related formulations.
reconstruction: The marginal attachment is unresolved. In particular, the separatedness conclusion on 26 cannot hold for arbitrary nonseparated P; the letter includes separatedness explicitly.
check_reason: The relative formulation is real; the exact omitted hypothesis must not be guessed.
